summary:
KRODHAVO is a planetary geospatial intelligence and multi-objective decision-support application that assists with strategic surface exploration on Mars. It analyzes NASA's Mars Global Surveyor (MGS) MOLA MEGDR-128 elevation data set to generate surface slope, relief, and a Terrain Difficulty Index for the planet. KRODHAVO uses an analytical framework of these parameters to classify the terrain according to low, moderate, and high difficulty. The program has a Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) framework to analyze and rank potential exploration routes with regard to four parameters: terrain accessibility, scientific worthiness, efficiency of traverse, and confidence of data. There are four regions of Mars to be explored: Jezero Crater, Gale Crater, Valles Marineris, and Olympus Mons.
Alongside the analytical framework, KRODHAVO provides a number of additional features, including an interactive map of Mars, planetary information display, location-based exploration and a story-driven chapter-based interface about a fictitious crew's journey through the Martian landscape. All these tools allow to connect the scientific information with the exploration interface. Overall, KRODHAVO tries to combine the elements of planetary elevation analysis, terrain intelligence, interactive visualization and multi-objective route evaluation to overcome the gap between the orbital data and the Mars surface exploration planning.
details:
1. Overview

KRODHAVO is a web-based planetary exploration platform developed to make Martian geospatial data more accessible and useful for understanding surface exploration challenges. It combines planetary mapping, topographic analysis, terrain intelligence, multi-criteria decision analysis, interactive exploration, and scientific storytelling.

2. Scientific Data & Technical Framework

The scientific foundation of KRODHAVO uses NASA's Mars Global Surveyor (MGS) Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA) MEGDR-128 elevation dataset, referenced to the IAU/IAG 2000 Mars coordinate system.

Topographic Analysis:

  • Elevation Analysis: Uses numerical planetary elevation data to investigate the Martian surface.
  • Slope Calculation: Applies Horn's 3×3 weighted finite-difference method to calculate surface gradients using surrounding elevation measurements.
  • Local Relief: Measures elevation variation within a surrounding terrain area.
  • Terrain Difficulty Index (TDI): Combines normalized slope (70%) and local relief (30%) into a score ranging from 0 to 100, classifying terrain into low, moderate, and high difficulty categories.

3. Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA)

KRODHAVO incorporates a Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis framework to evaluate and rank potential exploration routes. Rather than selecting routes based solely on distance, it considers four major factors:

  • Terrain Accessibility (35%)
  • Scientific Value (35%)
  • Traverse Efficiency (20%)
  • Data Confidence (10%)

Under the balanced evaluation strategy, these weighted factors are combined to calculate comparative route scores and support transparent exploration decisions. The framework also considers operational constraints, including maximum allowable slope, distance budgets, and mandatory scientific destinations.

4. Interactive Exploration

Beyond its analytical framework, KRODHAVO provides an interactive environment for exploring Mars. The website incorporates planetary mapping, location-based exploration, scientific information displays, and interactive visualizations, allowing users to investigate different Martian regions and understand their geological significance.

One of its distinctive features is an immersive, chapter-based storytelling experience called The Marswalk. It follows a fictional expedition crew, ARES, across Jezero Crater, Gale Crater, and Valles Marineris. Through cinematic environments, character dialogue, and mission-inspired narratives, it introduces real scientific concepts, including ancient Martian water systems, geological history, terrain uncertainty, and the challenges of route selection.

5. Implementation, Innovation & Impact

KRODHAVO combines planetary science, geospatial data, mathematical modelling, interactive web development, and scientific storytelling. Our development approach focuses on making complex planetary information understandable while maintaining transparency in the underlying analytical framework.

Its central innovation is the integration of planetary topographic information with terrain intelligence and multi-objective decision analysis in an accessible interactive platform.

KRODHAVO aims to support students, researchers, planetary science enthusiasts, and future mission planners in understanding Martian environments and the challenges associated with surface exploration.

The platform is designed as a research and decision-support tool, not a replacement for operational rover navigation or mission safety systems.
